On 20 June 1898 the US cruiser Charleston entered Apra Harbor and fired on an old fort. The Spanish governor, who had not heard that the Spanish-American War had begun, came out to apologise for not returning the salute, and was told he was a prisoner. He surrendered the next day.

Spain gave Guam to the United States by treaty that year and sold the other Mariana Islands to Germany. Guam was split from its neighbours.

The US Navy ran Guam as a naval station for half a century. Japan seized it in 1941, and the US retook it in the Battle of Guam in 1944.
